correctness.rationale: The proof fully defines the signed-cycle family, edge signs, IC(0) ordering, and exact arithmetic. Diagonal gauge yields a complete eigenvalue classification; retaining only existing edges yields sign-independent pivot recurrences. Continuant identities give p_j=D_j/D_{j-1} for j<n and p_n=D_{n+1}/D_{n-1}. Path eigenvalue zero locations give sharp signs and both endpoints, while scaling and monotone eigenvalue ratio establish shift and condition-number boundaries. Analytic Taylor expansion proves asymptotics. 3,667 checks in verify_cycle_ic.py test rational recurrences, direct IC and numerical eigenvalues, shifts, and asymptotic constants, without being substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed statement is an exact, complete two-class phase diagram for uniform-magnitude signed cycles under fixed-order IC(0), including the path-length-(n+1) determinant identity, the sharp first failed pivot, and exact rescue shift and conditioning boundary. The motivating 2024 primary work treats generic breakdown mechanisms and shifts, not this signed-cycle classification; a 2012 preconditioning survey treats M-matrix safety and the possibility of SPD breakdown. General algorithms and existence examples do not directly supply the two sign-class sharp formulas. Published-record semantic searches did not surface an equivalent or stronger statement; incomplete older-source access leaves a priority risk.

value.rationale: The complete sign-parity classification is a natural sharp boundary of sparse positive-definite factorization on the smallest family with nontrivial fill. It identifies when SPD plus fixed sparsity is insufficient, the exact pivot and parameter responsible, the smallest global-shift infimum that repairs it, and a quantitative condition-number threshold across every n. These are interpretable benchmarks for robust sparse preconditioner design. It does not claim a new generic incomplete-factorization method or finite-precision performance.
